intro: South Sudan is the world's newest country, independent since 2011 after decades of war with Sudan.

chapters.title: Nilotic peoples
text: Dinka, Nuer, Shilluk, Azande and many other peoples have lived along the White Nile and its swamps for centuries, mostly as cattle herders and farmers.

chapters.title: Part of Sudan
text: Under Anglo-Egyptian rule the south was run separately. After Sudan's independence in 1956, southerners fought two long civil wars against the northern government, in which about two million people died.

chapters.title: Independence and conflict
text: In a 2011 referendum, almost 99% of southerners voted to separate, and South Sudan became independent on 9 July 2011. A civil war broke out in 2013 between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and Vice-President Riek Machar. A 2018 peace deal brought a fragile unity government, but tensions rose again in 2025.

highlight.title: Newest country
highlight.text: South Sudan is the most recent country to join the United Nations.
